topics.topic: Behavior when only a misspelt service-token variable is supplied
questions: When the only attempted service-token setting is a misspelt unknown variable, must Registry fail because a token was apparently intended, or ignore it and start owner-only because all four declared service tokens are absent?

If the owner supplies only a misspelt service-token variable, so that none of the four declared service-token items is present, does Registry start owner-only under the all-four-or-none rule, or stop because a misspelt name must stop the start?
Does a misspelt service-token variable stop the start when no correctly named service-token variable is present, or does Registry ignore it and make the otherwise valid start owner-only?

quotes:
a variable whose name names none of them —
   one beginning with `REGISTRY_` included — is neither read nor checked and
   does not stop the start

a misspelt
   name still stops the start, as the item it was meant to set is then
   missing

the service tokens all four
   or none — none makes an owner-only start, and some but not all fail on the
   first missing one in rule 1's order
judgement.divergence: With only `REGISTRY_PRESUPRO_TOKENN` supplied, Registry either ignores the unknown variable and starts owner-only because no declared service token is present, or stops and names the PresuPro token as missing; the owner and PresuPro notice.
judgement.why: The unknown-variable rule and the misspelling clause give opposite startup outcomes when the misspelling concerns an optional all-or-none service-token group.

witness.initial: Every required non-service item is valid, none of the four declared service-token variables is present, and `REGISTRY_PRESUPRO_TOKENN` is present.
events: The owner sets Registry's configuration on the host with the misspelt variable.
outcomes: The unknown variable is neither read nor checked; none of the four declared tokens is present, so Registry starts owner-only.
The misspelt name means the PresuPro token is missing, so Registry stops the start and names that item.
basis: An instance's configuration is set on its host, readable only by the owner and the Registry process: on the VPS the compose environment file, on a local instance the environment it is started with.

Registry checks the configuration when it starts and serves nothing until
   every check passes; a failed check stops the start with a diagnostic that
   names the failed item and never its value (R0-37).

one service token for each service of A09 — PresuPro, Client
   Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel (R0-20, R0-23) — or, for an owner-only
   start, none of the four

topics.topic: Exact case-sensitive environment-variable names and accepted aliases or service-name conversion
questions: What is the exact, case-sensitive environment-variable name for each listed item, and are any aliases accepted?
What exact environment-variable name denotes each listed item, and how are the four service names converted into variable names?

quotes:
The items are exactly these: the store's
   location; the backup location and the backup key (A18); the owner
   credential; one service token for each service of A09 — PresuPro, Client
   Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel (R0-20, R0-23) — or, for an owner-only
   start, none of the four
judgement.why: The exact case-sensitive environment-variable names and service-name encoding are configuration-contract and format details owned by State 6, while State 2 specifies the required items and their startup behavior.

topics.topic: Meaning of config and checks_passed when unknown variables are not examined
questions: Does config in this invariant mean the complete set of REGISTRY_ environment variables, including variables that must not be checked, or only the projection onto declared configuration items; and what does checks_passed mean for an unexamined variable?

Now that `config` includes unknown `REGISTRY_` variables which are deliberately not checked, does `checks_passed(config)` mean that checks passed for the declared items only, or that every member of `config` was checked?

quotes:
The configuration is a set of environment variables whose names begin
   with `REGISTRY_`, set as R0-23 says. Registry reads exactly the items
   below and no other variable: a variable whose name names none of them —
   one beginning with `REGISTRY_` included — is neither read nor checked and
   does not stop the start

Registry checks the configuration when it starts and serves nothing until
   every check passes
judgement.why: The normative rule and Required test 7 make checks_passed concern the declared items only: an undeclared variable is deliberately unexamined and cannot prevent serving.

topics.topic: Whether A21 security review must reopen after A17 changes and record new category outcomes
questions: After the latest A17 change, is the security review reopened, and if so what are the new outcomes for every category that names A17 before A21 may again say the review is performed?
After the new A17 change made since the latest security review, is A21 currently reopened, and what new review result covers the categories that reference A17?

quotes: 2. A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.
judgement.divergence: After the post-closure A17 change, A21 is either reopened until the categories naming A17 are reviewed again, or remains PERFORMED without that review; the security reviewer and release gate notice.
judgement.why: A17 changed after the text with which A21 was closed, so A21's reopening rule conflicts with the unchanged declaration that the review is performed.

bases.passage: 2. A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.

unsupported_sides: 2. A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.

witness.initial: A21 says `Security review: PERFORMED`, and its authentication_credential_abuse and secrets categories name A17.
events: The owner changes A17 so undeclared `REGISTRY_` variables are ignored.
The security reviewer evaluates A21 under rule 2.
A release gate reads A21's recorded status.
outcomes: A21 rule 2 reopens the review, so the affected categories require a new recorded review before it is performed again.
The unchanged `Security review: PERFORMED` status lets the design proceed without a review of the changed A17 behavior.
witness.observer: The security reviewer and a release gate relying on A21.
basis: 2. A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.
- authentication_credential_abuse: APPLICABLE; references: A09, A13, A17; affected: M11, owner credential, service tokens, sign-in, owner session cookie
- secrets: APPLICABLE; references: A14, A17, A18; affected: owner credential, service tokens, backup key, diagnostics, audit log

topics.topic: Whether Registry must receive named settings fields instead of reading environment variables directly
questions: The passage must name these environment-dependent launch settings as fields of the settings object supplied through the configuration module, rather than leave generated Registry code to read raw environment variables directly.
Replace the direct environment-variable path with named fields of the settings object, leaving environment access to the settings module.

quotes:
The configuration is a set of environment variables whose names begin
   with `REGISTRY_`, set as R0-23 says. Registry reads exactly the items
   below and no other variable
judgement.why: The passage makes Registry read environment-dependent launch values directly instead of naming fields supplied by the settings object through the configuration module.
judgement.rule:
Таблица выше —
исчерпывающий список путей значения, и у каждого из них своя форма: перечисление
называется адресом, константа поставщика — `the imported X constant`,
настройка — полем объекта настроек.

topics.topic: Required test coverage proving all undeclared variables are neither read nor checked
questions: What Required tests item must show that every undeclared variable is neither read nor checked, rather than merely showing that the single name REGISTRY_EXTRA does not stop one start?

quotes:
a variable whose name names none of them —
   one beginning with `REGISTRY_` included — is neither read nor checked and
   does not stop the start
judgement.why: No witness can give two text-permitted behaviors because the universal normative clause already forbids rejecting any undeclared variable; what is missing is a stated SPEC_STANDARD rule requiring the Required tests to enumerate or parameterize every member of that class.
